name: Marco Wagner

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, independent of AI firms, employers, unions, political parties and government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What happens on an ordinary shift?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I have answered billing calls and chats at the contact centre for twelve years. I know the common mistakes and can usually settle an account, though I am neither a lead nor the fastest agent. I finished secondary school and earn less than many people doing this job. I use the approved AI search every day to find older bill notes, then open the current ledger before promising a credit.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58. My partner Rosa packs orders at a bakery, and our grown children live on their own. We rent a flat and have about two weeks of expenses saved; Rosa’s shifts change with orders. There are few other centres near us. I want to work less eventually, but cannot name the income that would replace our wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell coworkers the search box is useful for finding an old charge, but the real account decides the refund. A polished sentence cannot return money by itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my calls should remain, yet we are always close to the next rent date. Rosa’s bakery hours vary, and two weeks saved does not make a quiet order month comfortable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep checking current bill lines before using an AI draft. In the first year Rosa and I will take lunch from home on workdays and put the money we used to spend at the café into the rent envelope.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel steady about my desk, anxious about the flat. A mild AI year is still a short-savings year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which account did search get wrong?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It pulled the previous tenant’s adjustment as if it belonged to the current customer. I checked the account date before I sent anything.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the children help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have their own rent and families. We share meals, but I will not count their wages in our plan.

say: I would use **AI search** only with current ledger checks.
I would stop a **wrong-tenant credit** before approval.
think: I expect my **billing calls** to remain.
I fear Rosa’s **variable shifts** and two weeks saved still leave rent exposed.
do: Keep checking **current bill lines** before AI drafts go out.
Bring **workday lunches** from home and save former café money for rent.
S0.quote: A polished sentence cannot return money by itself.
fieldNote: His **twelve years** bring experience without lead status.
Daily AI search does not replace **ledger checks**.
The **lunch cut** moves actual spending into a rent reserve.

steps.text: Keep checking current bill ledger before approving AI-drafted credits
Bring lunch from home instead of buying workday café meals
Put former café spending into a rent envelope

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor to count the people calling back after an automatic credit. If the easy bills move to software, agents need paid time for the hard corrections.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can learn the new reviewer, but even a small rota cut would touch our rent. My long service does not mean the centre will keep every paid hour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will learn the new AI correction screen on twenty closed disputes during paid time and count reopened accounts. I will join three coworkers in asking management for written paid appeal hours and a rota before easy chats move. In the first year, if my hours fall, I will look at posted paid billing jobs nearby only where the full weekly wage covers rent and utilities.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious about losing hours. Knowing where the tool fails gives the group something more than a complaint.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the group ask together?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would sign one letter asking for paid correction time and a way customers can call a person. The reopened bills would go with the letter.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you check in another job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the whole paid week and compare the bus fare. A better hourly number can leave less rent money after travel.

say: I would count **reopened credits** after automated answers and show how often a customer needs another call.
I would seek **paid appeal hours** with coworkers.
think: I can learn **AI correction** but still lose shifts.
I know **service years** do not protect every paid hour.
do: Learn **AI correction screen** on twenty closed disputes during paid time.
Ask with **coworkers** for written paid appeal hours and human access.
Seek **posted paid billing work** after cuts with rent-and-utilities-covering weekly wages after bus fare.
S1.quote: A better hourly number can leave less rent money after travel.
fieldNote: The **joint letter** is shared worker action, not just a test presentation.
He tests a **new AI screen** beyond daily search.
Bus fare matters to **net rent money**.

steps.text: Learn new AI correction screen on twenty closed disputes during paid time
Sign with coworkers for written paid appeal hours and a human callback route
Seek posted billing work after cuts with weekly rent-and-utilities-covering pay net of bus fare

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say full thinking AI by 2028 could answer nearly every billing call, even the tangled ones. Robots around 2031 do not give our headsets extra time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect this queue could close. Two weeks saved and Rosa’s uncertain bakery shifts will not pay rent while I wait for another desk.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask for written staffing dates and put our planned new television aside. If my calls end in the first year after 2028, I will apply for posted paid library-circulation shifts as a short bridge; I will take one only when its weekly wages and hours cover rent and bus fare. I will keep the current calls as long as the centre pays for them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed. There is almost no gap between our savings and next month’s rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the library?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I volunteer to shelve books there once a month, but that is not a paid job. I would ask the library for an actual posted shift rather than use volunteering as a wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask for public help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If we were short of rent, I would check what local support exists instead of hiding the letter. I cannot budget local rent support until I know whether we qualify.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** could take billing calls.
I would say **2031 robots** do not delay desk risk.
think: I know two weeks saved and Rosa’s **variable wage** cannot bridge a long rent gap.
do: Request **written staffing dates**, defer television and keep paid calls while the centre offers shifts.
Apply for **posted paid library shifts** after call closure; take one only if weekly wages and hours cover rent and bus fare.
Check **local rent support** if a shortfall actually occurs.
S2.quote: I cannot budget local rent support until I know whether we qualify.
fieldNote: Library shelving is **voluntary**, not a paid vacancy.
He cannot count **public support** before knowing eligibility.
The library role is a **paid bridge**, not AGI-proof work.

steps.text: Delay buying a new television while rent is exposed
Apply for posted paid library shifts; take only with weekly wages/hours covering rent and bus
Check local rent support only if a real shortfall appears, without budgeting unconfirmed help
Keep taking paid billing calls while centre offers shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives us time to ask for real jobs and paid training before calls disappear. General AI reaches billing in 2031, with hands-on robots following around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn the library desk while I still earn at the centre, but I cannot buy an uncertain course from two weeks of savings. I would rather see the work first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep my calls and ask the library for the weekly rota of any posted paid circulation opening. If one appears and pays enough after bus fare to cover rent and utilities, I will learn its lending rules during paid hours. In the first year after 2031 I will move only if those paid shifts are actually available, while Rosa keeps her bakery work if possible.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but the extra years help me ask better questions. A volunteer badge will not pay the power bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take formal training?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if a real paid role requires it and the library funds my time. I am not signing up for an unpaid course before it posts a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does Rosa think?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Rosa and I would compare both weekly rotas before I changed desks. If the new bus trip ends after hers, we still need a way to get home.

say: I would ask for **posted paid library** hours before treating volunteer shelving as an income route.
I would separate **2031 billing** from later robots.
think: I could learn **lending rules** while current wages arrive.
I cannot fund **uncertain study** from two weeks saved.
do: Keep **paid billing calls**; move after 2031 only to available library shifts fitting Rosa’s rota and ride home, bakery work if possible.
Learn **library lending rules** on paid time only for a posted paid role covering rent and utilities after bus fare.
Take **required formal course** only for a posted paid library role that funds study time.
feel: **Anxious**, with time to inspect a real route.
S3.quote: A volunteer badge will not pay the power bill.
fieldNote: Paid library work needs a **posted rota**, not a volunteer badge.
Both **household rotas** and bus travel matter.
Any formal course needs a **real vacancy** and funded time.

steps.text: Keep taking paid billing calls while the centre offers shifts
Learn lending rules on paid time for posted paid role covering rent/utilities after bus fare
Move after 2031 only to available paid shifts fitting Rosa’s rota and a ride home
Take role-required formal course only for posted paid library job funding study time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues a decade is time to get written hours and keep a human route for wrong bills. General AI reaches calls in 2036 and robots follow hands-on work around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I may wish to work less, but I cannot say what would replace my wage. Two weeks saved makes this year’s rent a harder question than retirement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep my billing calls, bring lunch from home and set aside the café money. I will ask with coworkers once a year for written paid correction hours. In the first year after 2036, if my hours fall, I will apply for posted paid library or billing work only where the weekly net wages cover rent and utilities.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the next rent letter, even with ten years in the picture. A long warning does not grow a savings account by itself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if retirement comes sooner?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We have no settled income for it. I would not resign or count a pension figure I have never confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What about the grown children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They can visit for lunch, but their wages belong to their own households. Rosa and I plan from the pay we can see.

say: I would seek **written paid correction hours** each year through a joint coworker request.
I would distinguish **2036 calls** from later robots.
think: I cannot name a **replacement wage at 68**.
I know two weeks saved keeps **current rent** urgent even with a decade before AGI.
do: Keep **billing calls** and save former café spending.
Join coworkers’ yearly request for **paid correction hours**.
Seek **posted paid work** in library or billing after cuts with net weekly rent-and-utilities-covering wages.
feel: **Anxious** about present rent despite more preparation time.
S4.quote: A long warning does not grow a savings account by itself.
fieldNote: The **lunch saving** is actual new cash, not retained money.
He assumes **no pension** or adult-child subsidy.
The group asks for **paid hours**, not merely error data.

steps.text: Keep taking paid billing calls while available
Bring lunch from home and put former café cost toward rent
Ask with coworkers yearly for written paid correction hours
Seek posted paid library or billing shifts after cuts with net wages covering rent and utilities

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. I cannot pay rent through a long search with two weeks saved. Written notice, real posted work with full-week wages and a shared route to paid correction hours would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who reopens an account when the assistant has sent a wrong credit. The customer has a bill, not a debate about whether the first answer sounded convincing. Someone needs paid time to correct it.

headlineQuote: The customer has a bill, not a debate about whether the first answer sounded convincing.
portrait: Marco is a **58-year-old experienced agent** with secondary schooling, average skill and lower pay.
He uses **AI daily** but checks current ledgers; his partner’s bakery shifts vary.
With **two weeks saved** and few nearby centres, even a mild world leaves rent exposed.
He joins **paid-hour demands** and treats library volunteering as distinct from a posted paid job.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could close the billing queue before he finds rent-covering work.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, posted full-week work and shared demands for paid correction hours would help.
